ubānum: finger: ubānam ušatrīṣma “he made a finger point (at)” (the idiom for an accusation); ubānum, ubānam
tarāṣum-Š: to stretch out, point (Š-stem, causative “make point”): ušatrīṣma “he made (it) point”; the t is part of the root; with ubānam, “to point a finger at, accuse”
muttatum: half, a half-part: muttat “half of” (construct), muttassu “his half” (written mu-ut-ta-zu, ZU for -šu after the t). In §127 the thing halved is not written (his hair is understood); in §137, “half of the field, orchard and goods”
zinništum: woman (written with the single sign SAL, ŠAL in Harper): zinništam, zinništim, zinništum
zikārum: male, man as a sex (opposed to a woman): zikaram, zikārim “a male”
itūlum: to lie down, lie with: ittatīlma “he has lain, and” (perfect, in the -ma chain, §130); infinitive itūlim, utūlim “lying” (Harper prints both i-tu-lim and u-tu-lim), in “caught lying with another male”
ṣabātum-N: to be seized, caught (N-stem, passive of ṣabātum): iṣṣabit “she was caught” (preterite, in lā iṣṣabit); ittaṣbat “she was caught” (perfect)
kasûm: to bind, tie up (probable, not certain; Harper’s i-ka-zu has the ZU sign, read su): ikassûšunūtima “they shall bind them” (-šunūti “them”, -ma “and”)
balāṭum-D: to let live, keep alive (D-stem, factitive of balāṭum “to live”): uballaṭ “he lets (her) live”
kabālum-D: UNCERTAIN: to bind, hold fast, force (D-stem): ukabbilšima “he has held her down, and” (u-kab-bil-ši-ma, with -ši “her” and -ma); “held down” is the sense taken from the context
sūnum: lap, bosom: sūniša “her lap” (written zu-ni-ša); ina sūniša ittatīl “he lay in her lap”
mutum: husband (short u; Harper “husband”; mūtum “death” is another word, spelled the same, so the sense rests on context): mutiša “her husband”, mussa “her husband” (written mu-za, -ša after the t), mut “husband of” (construct; mut libbiša “the husband of her heart”)
tarāṣum-N: UNCERTAIN: to be stretched out, pointed at (N-stem, passive of tarāṣum): ittariṣma “it was pointed (at), and” (said of the finger, ubānum, the subject); the idiom means “has been accused”; the stem is read from the form and the sense
šalālum-N: to be carried off (as booty; said of a man taken away): iššalilma “he was carried off, and” (N-stem preterite, with -ma); the G-stem šalālum is “to plunder, carry off”
akālum: to eat; infinitive akālum “eating, food”: akālim “of eating”, in ša akālim ibašši “there is food” (literally “something of eating”)
pagrum: UNCERTAIN (a restoration): body, person: pagarša “her body, herself”, only in the broken lines XXII 14 and 19, where Harper restores [pa-gar-š]a; Harper “body”. Kohler–Ungnad restore “her property” in the same place, so the word is not on the stone
ḫāwirum: UNCERTAIN: husband (Harper ḫāwirum, from a root also read ḫāʾirum): ḫāwiriša “her husband”, at §135 the husband she had before (so Ungnad’s 1909 glossary: the first husband a girl marries); a rarer word than mutum
nabātum: to flee, run away (G-stem): ittabit “he fled”
zêrum: to hate, loathe: izīrūma “he hated, and” (preterite izīr + the subjunctive -u after aššum + -ma, in “he hated his city and fled”); the reading rests on the context
nabātum-N: UNCERTAIN: N-stem of nabātum “to flee”: innabitu “(that he) fled” (innabit + the subjunctive -u, after aššum); the stem is read from the form and is not secure
munnabtum: fugitive, runaway: munnabtim “of a fugitive”, in aššat munnabtim “the wife of a fugitive” (Harper’s mu-na-ab-tim); a noun formed from nabātum, understood from the sense
šugītum: UNCERTAIN: a class of woman named in §137, written {šal}šu-gi₄-tim (Harper prints šu-ge-tim): šugītim “(to) a šugītum”; the law sets her beside an ordinary wife as a woman who may bear children; her exact status is not known
rašûm-Š: to cause to acquire (Š-stem of rašûm “to acquire, get”; double accusative): ušaršušu (u-šar-šu-šu) “who has made him acquire (children)” (ušarši + the subjunctive -u + -šu “him”); the analysis of the ending is UNCERTAIN
šeriqtum: dowry, what the bride brings from her father’s house (§138 ša ištu bīt abiša ublam “which she brought from her father’s house”): šeriqtam “the dowry”, šeriqtaša “her dowry”. Harper reads it with q (še-ri-iq-ta-ša, the sign IG read iq) and later editions with k; UNCERTAIN in the form, the meaning rests on §138
-šim: to her, for her (dative suffix -šim, on a verb; the feminine counterpart of -šum): inaddiššim “he shall give her”, utarrūšim “they shall return to her”, inaddinūšimma “they shall give her, and”, ušallamšimma “he shall make (it) whole for her, and”; not the accusative -ši “her” of ukabbilšima and ubbiršima
aplum: heir, son as heir (Harper aplu; spelled ab-lim, the sign read ab or ap): aplim “of an heir”, in kīma aplim ištēn “like one heir”
tirḫatum: bride-price, the marriage payment (understood as the groom’s gift): tirḫatum “the bride-price”, tirḫatiša “her bride-price”
uzubbûm: UNCERTAIN: divorce payment, severance (uzubbûm): ana uzubbîm “as a divorce payment” (u-zu-ub-bi-im, genitive after ana); the reading is Harper’s and the word is rare

__broaden__.ugbabtum: UNCERTAIN: a priestess, written ŠAL.NIN.AN (Harper aššatum NIN.AN; NIN.AN is later written NIN.DINGIR, “lady of the god”); Harper gives no reading and translates only “a priestess”, later editions read ugbabtum, and the ŠAL may be only the woman-sign. The reading rests on the sign group and the context, not on a spelled word · here (§127) NIN.AN alone, with no ŠAL before it: ugbabtim “of a priestess”, still read ugbabtum, UNCERTAIN as before (Harper gives no reading)
__broaden__.abārum: to accuse; D-stem ubburum: ubbirma “he accused”, mubbirum “accuser” · utebbir (u-te-ib-bi-ir, Dt preterite, Harper’s stem II,2, the reflexive of the D-stem) “he has made a claim against” (Harper: “to file a claim for”) · ubbiršima “he accused her” (u-ub-bi-ir-ši-ma, D-stem preterite with -ši “her” and -ma)
__broaden__.ṣabātum: to seize: iṣṣabat, ṣabtu · stative with the subjunctive -u: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” (with Harper’s kirûm: “as long as the orchard is held”) · iṣṣabtamma (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tam-ma) “she seized (them), and” (perfect with the ventive -am and -ma): lā iṣṣabtamma “and she did not seize” · iṣbassuma (iṣ-ba-zu-ma, ZU for -ssu) “it seized him, and” (preterite iṣbat + -šu + -ma), of a debt seizing a man · iṣṣabtūšu (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tu-šu) “they seized him” (perfect, plural, with -šu “him”); iṣṣabat (iṣ-ṣa-ba-at) “he has seized (his wife)” (perfect)
__broaden__.zittum: share, portion (written ḪA.LA): zittašu, zittišu “his share” · zittam (ṣi-it-tam, the ZI sign read ṣi by Harper and zi here, as in ezēbim) “a share”: zittam kīma aplim ištēn “a share like one heir’s”
